diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the last term, we can write $Y_t=z+n_{T-t}(Y_t)$ and expand

issues.failure_explanation: Since Y_t = z + n with z = Pi(Y_t), <n, Y_t> = <n, z> + ||n||^2. Normality of n to the tangent space at z does not make <n, z> vanish, because z is a position vector, not a tangent vector. The term 2<n,z> is dropped. It vanishes only for special geometries such as a ridge through the origin, and it is unbounded when the ridge is unbounded.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the term 2<n,z> <= 2 rho ||z|| and bound ||z|| on the relevant (bounded) portion of the ridge, adding a localization argument. The extra rho*R-type source then enters B_{s,t} and the final rate.
issues.overall_effect: The differential inequality for E[D] and hence the normal-alignment bound and floor are unsupported for general data.
issues.title: Normal drift computation wrongly sets <n, Y_t> = ||n||^2
issues.why_classification: A contained extra estimate plus localization is needed. The result survives in comparable form with a modified source term.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, $Y_t$ (or $\Tilde{Y}_t$) satisfies the \eqref{eq:sufficient closeness} with probability $1$ as $t\to T^-$.
the union of all center-dominated regions covers almost every point in the space and $\Tilde{Y}_t$ enters it.
samples cease sliding toward data and instead diffuse on ridges, enabling generalization.

issues.failure_explanation: The derivative bound (via Lemma lem:application closeness) holds only while the path stays in B^(i) for a fixed i. A pathwise condition is mixed with a bound on an expectation. Gronwall is then applied on all of [t_in, T-delta]. The supporting claim that the process enters a center region with probability 1 is false: the left side of the sufficient-closeness condition can be zero (points equidistant from centers). The paper itself asserts that samples remain spread along inter-mode ridges.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must introduce stopping times and conditioning on remaining in a fixed B^(i), and bound the probability of that event for the learned dynamics Y~_t.
issues.overall_effect: The tangent-sliding bound and the tangent-error floor are not established for the regime the paper studies (inter-mode generation).
issues.title: Tangent contraction integrated over times where the center-region hypothesis fails
issues.why_classification: A central guarantee loses its validity in the advertised regime, and a new probabilistic argument is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: matrix consisting of orthonormal columns as the top-$d^*$ eigenvectors of $\nabla^2\log p_{T-t}(m_{T-t}^{(i)})$

issues.failure_explanation: At a center, Sigma = O(theta), so all Hessian eigenvalues are within O(theta/h^2) of -1/h. The gap between lambda_{d*} and lambda_{d*+1} is therefore exponentially small. The top-d* eigenvectors and their time derivative are governed by perturbation over the gap, so theta cancels and the claimed O(theta poly) bound on P dP (I-P) has no support. The frame U may even be ill-defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit eigen-gap assumption at the centers, or define the tangent frame from the ridge tangent space, and redo the frame-derivative estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The O(1) control of the frame-motion term in the tangent inequality is unsupported.
issues.title: Frame-derivative bound ignores degenerate eigen-gap at centers
issues.why_classification: A contained new estimate or hypothesis is needed. The tangent result can survive in comparable form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the normal and tangential mean-errors scale like $\delta^c \int_\delta^{T-\tilde{t}_{\mathrm{in}}} h_t^{1-c}/{w(t)} \dee t$
$w(t)=1$ produces the smallest tangent errors, while $w(t)=h_t$ and $w(t)=h_t^2$ lead to progressively larger errors.

issues.failure_explanation: Evaluating the stated integrals with h_t ~ 2t gives the following. Normal: O(1) for w=h^2, O(delta^c) for w=h, and O(delta^c) for w=1. Tangent: O(1), O(delta^{1/2}), and O(delta^{1/2}). The claimed O(delta) and O(delta^2) do not follow. The integrals as stated give the same order for w=h and w=1, so they do not support the claimed ordering of inductive biases or the experimental interpretation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the rates to O(1), O(delta^c or delta^{1/2}), and O(delta^c or delta^{1/2}), and withdraw or re-argue the distinction between w=1 and w=h.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical explanation of weight-dependent generation, and its claimed agreement with the experiments, is unsupported.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $2\eta{\|\Tilde{U}\|}\le 1$, the gradient descent is stable.

issues.failure_explanation: The iteration contracts by the factor (1 - 2 eta lambda_j), which requires eta < 1/lambda_1. For eta in [1/lambda_1, 2/lambda_1), |1 - 2 eta lambda_1| can exceed 1 (down to -3), so the iterates diverge. Err_train(k) then grows rather than decaying geometrically, and A_k does not converge to A_infinity.
issues.overall_effect: The geometric-decay and convergence claims fail on part of the stated step-size range.
issues.title: Step-size condition eta < 2/lambda_1 does not ensure GD convergence
issues.why_classification: A local hypothesis change preserves all conclusions and rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\mc{B}_{t}^{(i)}(\theta_{t})$ is defined in \eqref{eq:data dominate region} with any $\theta_t=\exp(- o(h_{t}^{-1}) )$.

issues.failure_explanation: First, reach is also limited by global bottlenecks between ridge components, not by curvature alone. Second, the theta-small third-derivative bound holds only on center-dominated regions. Ridge points between modes (e.g., near the midpoint in the two-point example) lie outside those regions, where ||nabla^3 log p|| is of order R^3/h^3 with no theta factor. Taking a sup over the closure of the union does not justify the bound, so the bound r_t = Omega(beta h^3/(theta R^3)) is unsupported. The same out-of-region bound is used for the cubic Taylor term in the stage-2 proof.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must bound the third derivative and the global reach on the whole ridge, including the inter-mode segments, and propagate the resulting (likely smaller) r_t through stages 1 and 2.
issues.overall_effect: The tube radius, the projection-motion bounds, the stage-1 entry probability and the normal-contraction constants all lose their justification.
